name: Mock Aptitude Test
subtitle: UVTN 2022 · Round 1: CV & Aptitude Test
description: Full-length mock round: 9 verbal reasoning, 10 quantitative reasoning (the easyAirways case) and 6 abstract reasoning questions in one 30-minute sitting, with the official answer key and written explanations in the review.
keyNote: Official answer key and explanations from the Mock Aptitude Test answer key file.

g12.title: Questions 12, 13 and 14: easyAirways
g12.intro:
easyAirways is a company that runs airline services across all major cities in Europe. Its main hub is located in the United Kingdom in London. easyAirways provides two types of services:
1. Passenger services: easyAirways provides air transport services for passengers traveling between major capitals in Europe. Most of the company’s flights link London to other urban centres.
2. Cargo services: easyAirways’s cargo business is dedicated to the transportation of goods by air. The company operates fixed routes within Europe. Businesses purchase volume in its planes to have their goods transported between airports.
The company’s passenger service was designed to offer low-cost tickets on short haul European flights by cutting down on complimentary services such as drinks and food. It was initially targeted to young holidaymakers who are particularly price sensitive. But, over the past few years, an increasing share of its passenger tickets has been sold to professionals as an economic crisis has hit Europe. As the company’s ties with businesses have developed it has launched a new cargo service to transport goods between airports.
easyAirways has found that there are considerable variations in profitability between the different routes it operates as well as between its passenger and cargo businesses. Table 1 shows a summary of the analysis carried out by the CEO’s team so far.
g12.note: The founder of easyAirways has decided to sell his shares in the company on the stock market. In order to prepare for the company’s IPO, he wants to optimise the profitability of all the routes operated by the airline. He has hired your team to study the company’s portfolio of routes and to make recommendations to improve the least profitable routes.

g16.title: Questions 16, 17 and 18: maintenance costs
g16.intro:
In an effort to further improve the profitability, the team then investigates if there is any scope to reduce costs at the airline. One of the CEO’s questions is whether his team of aircraft maintenance engineers could be organized in a more cost-efficient way than it currently is.
Aircraft maintenance engineers are licensed professionals who perform a series of tasks from an approved maintenance schedule to ensure the safety of the aircraft and its passengers. These tasks are typically carried out between a plane’s landing and its next take-off. They include checking the tire pressure, inspecting fluid leaks, looking at potential damage to the aircraft structure, etc. The team is in charge of taking the necessary steps to restore the aircraft to safe condition before it takes off again.
During a discussion with the Chief Maintenance Engineer, you find out the following information about the maintenance of aircrafts in London for the three routes displayed in Table 1:
• Senior maintenance engineers are not allowed to work more than 12 hours per day and 48 hours per week for safety reasons
• At least two senior maintenance engineers need to be on-site at all times to supervise the 10 junior engineers maintaining easyAirways planes
• On occasions, maintenance aircraft engineers need to work overtime to deal with special maintenance operations
• Labor costs for maintenance operations amount to £4 million per annum for the three routes. The quarterly number of maintenance operations is 390

questions.intro: Nobody knows what life forms may exist outside our own planet. The search for extraterrestrial life in the universe took a step nearer to fruition with the discovery in June of what are believed to be traces of water on the surface of Mars. Life on our planet requires water and its presence on Mars may point towards the existence of past life on the planet. The Phoenix Mars Lander robot landed on the plains of Mars on May 25th 2008, searching for signs that the Martian environment might once have been habitable to life. When it dug a ditch in the planet’s surface, photos revealed small patches of bright material. Four days later those patches had disappeared, causing scientists to speculate that they were water ice that had previously been buried and which vaporised when exposed to the air. Scientists insisted that if the patches had been salt, they wouldn’t have disappeared and if they had been solid carbon dioxide, then they wouldn’t have vaporised.
questions.stem: Statement: The Phoenix Mars Lander has provided proof that life once existed on Mars.
Statement: Since the Phoenix Mars Lander cannot excavate it is limited to surface photography.

The shocking discovery of cheating on the most common college entrance examination should not affect the reputation of the National Testing Center. **The revelation confirms that the system works,** since the students themselves were the ones who reported their peers for unethical behavior.
The portions in bold play which of the following roles in the argument?
options: It is a claim for which the argument gives evidence, and which is used to support the primary claim.
It is the argument’s main position, and another conclusion provides support for it.
It is an assumption that has no stated evidence in the argument.
It is the primary conclusion of the argument.
It is a statement that contains both a premise and an assumption that support the conclusion.

questions.stem:
Running shoes have to be replaced periodically due to the repeated force of impact wearing down the sole and damaging the insole. High-tech running shoes which incorporate memory foam and gel inserts can adapt to the individual stride, last much longer, and contribute to improved running performance. However, the price of ordinary running shoes is much lower and casual runners do not get enough use out of high-tech shoes to justify the expense of the materials. Therefore, for most runners, high tech running shoes do not save money.
Which of the following would be most useful to know in evaluating the argument?
options: If there are shoe materials that improve running performance but are not as expensive as memory foam and gel inserts.
The length of time an ordinary running shoe and a high-tech one can be used before needing to be replaced.
Whether casual runners are interested in upgrading their running performance.
The difference between the price of materials typically being used in high-tech running shoes and that of materials being used in high-tech shoes tailored to other sports.
Whether the shoes would be used for any other sport or recreational activities besides running.

questions.stem:
A recent study of teenagers found that, contrary to predictions, a special nutritious eating diet does not have positive impacts on students’ academic performance. Fifty high school students, half of whom were given a nutritionally balanced diet, had grades no higher than those students who were not placed on the diet plan.
Which of the following, if true, is most useful in determining the accuracy of the study described above?
options: Teenagers who previously scored lower academically found that after they changed their diets, their grades improved dramatically.
Students who participated in various fitness activities found that their grades improved noticeably after they altered their exercise habits.
Performance of business executives was shown to improve drastically after major alterations were made in their diets.
Honors students, after altering their diets, maintained that they did not change their study habits.
All of the teenagers who volunteered for the study were either in their first or second year of high school.

questions.stem:
Recently, the new hiring requirements for policemen of city X have included drug testing and background check. Concurrently, there is a shortage of policemen. However, the shortage is not caused by the new hiring requirements. The true reason for it is the working conditions and low pay.
Which of the following, if true, would best support the claims above?
options: Several candidates withdrew from consideration after knowing about the new background checks.
Some of the current staff of policemen would not have been able to pass the new background check.
In recent years, policemen starting a new job with the city report higher levels of previous experience than in the past.
Tenured policemen believe the new hiring requirements have caused the shortage of policemen.
Policemen quitting their jobs have claimed that they are leaving because of low pay and safety concerns.

questions.stem:
Ken: Nostalgia is the only reason people like old clothes, old music, and old cars. Without nostalgia, people would always seek out the new because human beings instinctively prefer that which is new to that which is old.
Lola: I disagree. Your whole claim rests on a narrow and unsophisticated understanding of the word “new.” In matters of style, old can be seen as quite new.
Which of the following, if true, best explains Lola’s paradoxical claim?
options: In matters of style, anything that is a change from the present is considered new.
In matters of style, there is no difference between old and new.
Old clothes, music, and cars never really go out of style.
The executives who make style decisions for clothing, music, and car companies generally like the styles popular when they were young.
In matters of style, change is more important than timing.

questions.stem:
A student response survey found that students who paid for 15 or more in-person tutoring sessions on an hour-by-hour basis missed or rescheduled a session on average once every six sessions. By contrast, those students who purchased tutoring sessions in ten-hour packages missed or rescheduled a session on average only once every ten sessions. This indicates that students are at least partly motivated by the amount of money they have invested for in-person tutoring.
Which of the following, if true, calls into question the explanation above?
options: All students must pay a 10% fee for rescheduling any tutoring session, but if a student cancels a session entirely, the entire cost is forfeited.
Upon purchase of any tutoring hours, students are required to immediately schedule all the purchased hours.
Students who try to reschedule tutoring sessions without enough notice may not be able to make up the session in a timely fashion, so that it counts as a missed session.
The price per hour was slightly more expensive for those who bought individual hours.
Many students who missed or rescheduled sessions did so although they made a strong verbal commitment beforehand to be present.

questions.stem:
Online auction websites have become extremely popular in part because consumers are often able to buy items at significantly lower than retail prices. Although companies around the globe have been able to increase sales through these websites, furniture dealers have not enjoyed similar successes and should not continue to waste time trying to sell items online.
Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the conclusion above?
options: Some consumers prefer to shop in person.
Some consumers do not trust the security of the internet and therefore do not buy from these online auction sites.
Excessive shipping fees would erase any benefit the consumer sees from a lower price.
Portions of the population are not internet savvy.
A huge benefit to consumers purchasing furniture is the ability to view styles available from the comfort of their own home.

questions.stem:
The price per unit of product A increased by 10 percent over the same time period that the price per unit of product B decreased by 10 percent. The reduced price per unit of product B was what percent of the original price per unit of product A?
(1) The increased price per unit of product A was equal to the original price per unit of product B.
(2) The increase in the price per unit of product A was 10/11 the decrease in the price per unit of product B.

If a total of 320 students are attending two sections of the UVTN Kickstart Conference Day event, how many of the 320 students are juniors?
(1) 2/3 of the students in Section 1 are juniors.
(2) 1/2 of the students in Section 2 are seniors.

options: r < (2 x a x b x c + d x e x f) / 4
r = (2 x a x b x c + d x e x f) / 4
r < (2 x a x b x c + 2 x d x e x f) / 4
r = (2 x a x b x c + 2 x d x e x f) / 4

questions.stem: Which of the following statements CAN be concluded regarding the data in Table 1?
options: The Barcelona route has the lowest revenue potential for the passenger business
The Frankfurt route has the most actual profit across the passenger and cargo businesses
The cargo business generates 10% more profit than the passenger business overall
In these three cities, the passenger business delivers two to four times more profit per customer dollar spent than the cargo business

questions.stem: Which of the following arguments, if true, would NOT help explain the difference in the net profit margins for the passenger business across the three airline routes in Table 1?
options: There are differing levels in the average airport charges and taxes per flight in the three routes
The number of transportation options to reach the three cities from London differs
There are differing levels in the average fuel cost per flight paid in the different cities
There are differing levels in the average frequency of flights in the different cities

questions.intro:
Your team then decides to evaluate the exact number of seats that needs to be filled for each flight to break even on the Paris route. They gather the following information about the flight’s costs:
• The Paris route has got a dedicated crew of pilots and cabin attendants costing the airline £1.0 million per calendar year
• Over the past twelve months fuel costs have averaged out at £1,600 per flight from London to Paris, as well as from Paris to London
• The company leases the plane it uses for the Paris route for £20,000 per month
• All other airport and maintenance costs averaged out at £15,000 per month over the past twelve months
• No other costs are large enough to be considered
questions.stem: What is the SMALLEST number of passengers required for the airline to break even on a typical flight from London to Paris?
What is the average percentage of special maintenance operations in Q1 and Q2?
Based on the information provided by the Chief Maintenance Engineer, which of the following statements is a valid conclusion?
options: A total of eight senior maintenance engineers are sufficient to cover weekly shifts
Special maintenance operations account for more than 10% of maintenance related labor cost
Staff who are not senior maintenance engineers do not work more than 48 hours per week
The majority of labour maintenance costs are for staff who are not senior maintenance engineers

questions.stem: Assuming that regular maintenance operations and special maintenance operations have the same labour costs, which of the following numbers is closest to the average labour cost of a special maintenance operation?
options: £2,400 per special operation
£2,600 per special operation
£2,800 per special operation
£3,000 per special operation
